title: Desk Guidance: Customer-Pay Repairs Orders Held by One Customer
content:
**Rule.** A customer, individual or fleet, may hold any number of Customer-Pay Repairs repair orders across vehicles; there is no customer-level cap. The per-vehicle limit and the exclusion with insurance claim repairs are set by the Customer-Pay Repairs vehicle exclusivity rule.

## The rule restated

| Question | Answer under this rule |
|---|---|
| Is there a ceiling on how many Customer-Pay Repairs repair orders one customer holds? | No. There is no customer-level cap. |
| Does it matter whether the customer is an individual or a fleet account? | No. The rule is the same for both. |
| Over what are the orders counted? | Across the customer's vehicles. |
| What limits a single vehicle? | The per-vehicle limit and the exclusion with insurance claim repairs, which belong to the vehicle exclusivity rule, not to this one. |

## Illustration (hypothetical)

A fleet account has Customer-Pay Repairs repair orders open on four different vehicles. At the customer level the count of four meets no ceiling, because none exists; whether a given vehicle may carry an order is a per-vehicle question.
